I reviewed youtube.ts, google-provider.ts, google-errors.ts, media-source.ts, the youtube capability record and their tests, against the verified facts file. Most of the protocol is correct; there are four real defects, and the worst can upload the same video twice.

**What is correct:**
- **Session start:** URL, part, X-Upload headers and categoryId as a string are right, and privacyStatus, selfDeclaredMadeForKids and containsSyntheticMedia are always sent.
- **Chunks:** sizes are multiples of 262144, equal except the last, and the Content-Range math is right.
- **Status replies:** 308 with and without a Range header, resume via `bytes */N`, 404 treated as transient, and 201/200 parsing all behave as documented. I ran a local server to confirm that Node's fetch with redirect:'manual' returns the 308 with readable headers and sends Content-Length: 0 on the status check.
- **Identity and privacy:** youtube.readonly is requested for channels.list and videos.list, and an unticked readonly leads to "no postable accounts". Uploads are forced private until audited, with a notice and a videos.list read-back.
- **Validation:** title 100 characters, description 5000 bytes, no < or >.
- **Error mapping:** quotaExceeded is transient until the midnight Pacific reset; insufficientPermissions, accessNotConfigured, youtubeSignupRequired, uploadLimitExceeded and 401 each map to their own class and code.
- **OAuth:** the authorise URL parameters are right (space-joined scopes, access_type=offline, include_granted_scopes, prompt=consent, state). The exchange sends the secret in the body, parses granted scopes and refuses a reply with no refresh token. Refresh keeps the refresh token, and invalid_grant becomes a credential failure. Bundles work.

**Defects:**
- **High: duplicate upload.** If the reply to the final chunk is lost and the status checks keep failing for 15-30 s (or one 503 asks to wait over 60 s), the adapter reports a retryable "Nothing was published". The worker or a CLI re-run then uploads the whole video again. A scratch test ended with two videos on the fake channel. Once the project is audited and privacy is public, this is a duplicate public video.
- **Medium: long uploads cannot finish.** The token is never renewed during an upload, so a 401 restarts it from byte 0 with another hour-long token. An upload longer than an hour fails on all 6 worker attempts.
- **Low: false needs-reauth.** If the connection drops while the token reply is being read during a refresh, the error carries no failure class. The vault then marks the connection as needing reconnection.
- **Low: partial grant shown as ready.** A sign-in without youtube.upload is stored and listed as "ready", and every upload from it fails at the session start.

All 859 workspace tests pass, and the adapters package typechecks cleanly. No repository file was modified. The scratch tests that reproduce findings 1-3 are fetch308.mjs, final-chunk.test.ts, token-expiry.test.ts and refresh-body-error.test.ts, in C:\Users\RANAZA~1\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\d--My-AI-Works\2e482ace-b0b2-4185-962b-a49ffb3bed17\scratchpad\review.

I reviewed credential lifecycle, security and tenant isolation in commit range 88b9956..7303e89 of Social-Publisher, plus the three non-git folders. I found 3 defects worth reporting: 2 medium and 1 low. The vault does not hand over a fresh enough token for long YouTube uploads, and nothing renews it mid-upload. Connect reports success when the YouTube upload permission was not granted. Refresh failures that do not mean the token is dead still disable the channel and raise a false critical. Scratch tests under ...\scratchpad\review confirm all three. `pnpm -r test` passes: 0 failures across 10 packages.

Checked and correct:
- **Expiry column:** Google authorisations write null to expires_at at all three places that set it: saveProviderAuth, the vault's store, and the merged credential after a refresh. So refresh-cli does not list them, `expiredProviderAuths` and `markAuthExpired` never trigger on the hourly token, and `checkCredentialExpiry` stays quiet.
- **Merge on refresh:** `{...credential, ...refreshed}` keeps the refresh token, scopes and `authorisationExpiresAt`. `reviveDates` keeps a stored null as null. Transient refresh errors are re-thrown without marking anything.
- **Which token goes where:** the refresh token is copied only to accounts that publish with the same token (Google channels; Pinterest and LinkedIn copies are unused). Meta Pages get none. The Google externalUserId is the OIDC `sub`, so reconnecting updates the existing row.
- **Tenant isolation:** the provider-aware `resolveAuth` only looks at `listProviderAuths(user.tenantId)`. An account must be found by the authorisation it names. Connection upserts are keyed by (tenant, platform, account id). One tenant's or one provider's authorisation cannot be used for another's accounts.
- **Publish sites:** all four (worker, CLI post, MCP context, web engine) pass `adapter.refreshCredential`; only YouTube defines one. The monitor's token check covers Meta connections only.
- **Error mapping:** publish-service reports `NeedsReauthError` as 'credential' and carries the cause's code.
- **Tokens in transit:** the token goes only in the Authorization header. `isGoogleUrl` keeps it to googleapis.com. The client secret is sent only in the token request body to oauth2.googleapis.com.
- **Logs and records:** no token reaches an error message, the audit log or the console. No credential-shaped strings are in the diff or in LinkedIn-Content-Ops, LinkedIn-Content-System or Social-Render.
- **Redaction:** the ya29., 1// and GOCSPX- patterns catch tokens in URL queries, JSON and free-text messages. The only miss is a percent-encoded refresh token (1%2F%2F…), and no current code path logs one.

I found no critical or high regressions in the paths that are live today. The two findings above are a medium misreport and a low cosmetic one. Nothing was modified, and no live service, database or .env file was touched. confirmed.title: When the reply to the final chunk is lost, the adapter reports a retryable "Nothing was published", and the retry uploads the video a second time
confirmed.failure_scenario:
The adapter PUTs the last chunk of a video. For a file of 8 MiB or less this is the only chunk. YouTube receives every byte and creates the video, but the 201 reply never arrives (connection reset, Wi-Fi drop) or comes back as a 5xx.

1. #put turns the network error into {kind:'interrupted'} (lines 621-627). It keeps no record that the final byte range was already sent.
2. The `bytes */N` status checks then fail too. Any one of these is enough:
   - five backoffs pass (1, 2, 4, 8 and 16 s at most with full jitter, about 15-30 s of outage);
   - a single 503 carries Retry-After over 60 s (lines 571-577), which throws without asking for status at all;
   - a status check gets 401 or 404.
3. #sendFile throws failureClass 'transient' with "Nothing was published; the next attempt starts it again". The message also says "stopped at byte 0".
4. The retry comes from one of two places:
   - The worker retries the transient error (worker.ts:232-236). platformPostId is still null, so the guard at worker.ts:132 does not stop it.
   - The owner sees `[retryable]` in the CLI and runs it again.
5. The retry opens a NEW session and uploads the whole video again.

The result is two copies on the channel and another unit of the 100/day upload bucket spent. Once YOUTUBE_UPLOADS_AUDITED=true with public privacy, it is a duplicate public video. This breaks the file's own rule at lines 53-57: "nothing may throw once the video exists".

Scratch test scratchpad\review\final-chunk.test.ts uses a fake YouTube that creates the video when it has every byte, then drops the reply, then fails 5 status checks.
- First publish rejects with: `transient | The YouTube upload was interrupted 6 times in a row and stopped at byte 0 of 10000. Nothing was published; the next attempt starts it again.`
- A second publish then succeeds, and the fake channel holds `[ 'VID1', 'VID2' ]`.

The existing test youtube.test.ts:363-377 ('gives up after repeated interruptions') asserts this transient outcome for a single-chunk file whose only, and final, PUT got a 503.
confirmed.suggested_fix:
1. Record when a PUT that covers the last byte (`last === size - 1`) has been attempted without a definitive reply.
2. From then on, never throw a retryable "Nothing was published":
   - Keep polling `bytes */N` for longer, since it is cheap.
   - If the outcome still cannot be established, throw a non-retryable error with its own code. Its message says the video may already exist and to check YouTube Studio's uploads before posting again.
   - Apply this in every branch reached after the final chunk: attempts exhausted, Retry-After over 60 s, 401 or 404 on the status check, budget exhausted.
3. A more robust option: store the session URI with the target. The next attempt then asks the old session for its status before it opens a new one.
4. Change the youtube.test.ts:363-377 expectation, and add a test where the final chunk throws and the status checks fail; the result must not be transient.

check.reasoning:
I could not refute it. I checked the code and ran it.

**Evidence quotes are accurate.** In `youtube.ts:620-627` `#put` turns any fetch throw into `return { kind: 'interrupted' }`. Nothing records that the request covered the last byte, so `offset` stays where it was. Lines 553-568 then set `mustAsk = true`, increment `failures += 1`, and once `failures > this.#maxResumeAttempts` throw `failureClass: 'transient'` with "...stopped at byte ${offset}... Nothing was published; the next attempt starts it again."

Three other exits behave the same way:
- **Long Retry-After (lines 571-577):** `asked > LONGEST_INLINE_WAIT_MS` throws transient "Nothing was published" without asking the session for its status. This contradicts the docstring at lines 50-51 ("never assumed to have arrived or not").
- **404 on the status check (lines 654-660):** `#interpret` throws transient.
- **401 on the status check (lines 662-671):** `#interpret` throws transient.

**Nothing downstream stops the retry.**
- `publish-service.ts:195` sets `retryable: error.isRetryable`, and `errors.ts:57-59` returns true for 'transient'.
- `worker.ts:232` (`const shouldRetry = error.retryable && job.attempts < MAX_ATTEMPTS`, with `MAX_ATTEMPTS = 6`) reschedules the job. Its only guard is `worker.ts:132` (`if (target.platformPostId !== null)`), and that field is still null.
- `vault.withCredential` (`vault.ts:132-188`) neither retries nor dedupes.
- `publish()` opens a new session every time (line 334). No session URI is persisted and nothing checks the channel's recent uploads.
- `cli/post.ts:432` prints `[retryable]`. In the MCP path the network failure carries code `PLATFORM_UNREACHABLE`, whose fix text is "Retry — this is usually momentary".
- The existing test `youtube.test.ts:363-377` asserts the transient outcome for a single-chunk file whose only PUT is also its final PUT.

**Scratch test.** `scratchpad\review\skeptic-final-chunk.test.ts` uses the real adapter and the real PublishService, plus a loop that mirrors the worker's retry rule. The fake Google follows the documented protocol: the video exists once the session holds every byte, and a status query repeats the 201 (research A1 line 43).
- **Control:** reply lost, then a healthy status check. The adapter recovers VID1 and there is no duplicate, so the resume logic works when the network comes back quickly.
- **Lost reply plus 5 failed status checks:** the first attempt reports `transient retryable=true code=PLATFORM_UNREACHABLE | ...interrupted 6 times in a row and stopped at byte 0 of 10000. Nothing was published`. The real jittered backoffs added up to 14.4 s in this run, with a ceiling of 31 s. The retry succeeds and the channel holds `['VID1','VID2']`.
- **503 with Retry-After 120 on a committed final chunk:** zero status checks, retryable, two videos.
- **401 on the status check:** retryable, two videos.
- **3-chunk file:** the same result ("stopped at byte 524288 of 600000").

**Re-rated medium, not high.** The trigger needs a coincidence:
- **Network outage:** the reply must be lost in the short window after Google has committed the last chunk, and the outage must then last through 5 status checks. That is about 15-30 s when fetch fails fast, longer if connects hang until their timeout.
- **503 with a long Retry-After:** this only matters if Google commits a chunk and still answers 503, which is unverified.
- **401/404 on the status check:** rare for small files, because the vault refreshes tokens with a 5-minute margin.

Uploads are forced private until the audit, so today the result is a private duplicate. It also costs one of the 100 uploads/day, and the adapter says "Nothing was published" when the video exists. Once `YOUTUBE_UPLOADS_AUDITED=true` and privacy is public, the same path makes a duplicate public video, which is critical-class.

confirmed.title: An upload that runs longer than the access token's remaining life cannot finish: a 401 mid-upload restarts the whole video from byte 0
confirmed.failure_scenario:
The vault renews a token only when it is within 5 minutes of expiry (vault.ts:93), so a publish can start with anywhere from 5 to 60 minutes of token left. The adapter then has no way to renew mid-upload:
- it sends the same token on every chunk PUT (line 613);
- the publish context carries only the access token (publish-service.ts:171), so refreshCredential cannot be reached inside publish.

The adapter's own model (lines 663-665) is that the token can run out mid-upload. When it does, the 401 is thrown as transient, and the next attempt opens a brand-new session and starts again at byte 0. Two cases follow:
- (a) A 15-minute upload that starts with 10 minutes of token left fails at minute 10 and is redone from scratch.
- (b) Any upload longer than 60 minutes fails on every attempt, for example a 10 GB 4K video at 20 Mbps, well inside the declared 256 GB / 12 h capability. All 6 worker attempts (MAX_ATTEMPTS=6) end in 401. Each opens a new videos.insert session, likely a unit of the 100/day upload bucket each.

The next attempt renews it ... throw new PublishError('YouTube stopped accepting the access token partway through the upload, most likely because it expired. ' + 'Nothing was published; the next attempt renews the token and uploads again.', { failureClass: 'transient', httpStatus: status })`

Scratch test scratchpad\review\token-expiry.test.ts: 8 chunks at 10 simulated minutes each, with a fresh 60-minute token per attempt.

- `sessions opened: 6 restarts from byte 0: 6`
confirmed.suggested_fix:
1. Give the adapter a way to renew mid-upload, for example a `ctx.renewCredential()` callback that the caller backs with vault.withCredential plus refreshCredential.
2. On a 401 during #put: renew the token, ask the same session for its status (`bytes */N`), and continue from there instead of throwing.
3. At minimum:
   - start every YouTube upload with a token that has nearly its full hour (a larger refresh skew for this adapter);
   - store the session URI, so a retry resumes the upload rather than restarting it.

check.reasoning:
I could not refute the code side. The trigger depends on live Google behaviour that nobody has verified.

**Code side: confirmed by reading and by a scratch test.**
- **One token for the whole upload.** youtube.ts:613 sends `headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${ctx.credential.accessToken}`, ...headers }` on every chunk.

confirmed.title: Hosted schedule_post reports a YouTube post as scheduled even though it can never publish

No media_assets or post_media rows are written, so at the slot the worker rebuilds the draft with `media: []`. confirmed.failure_scenario: (PLAUSIBLE.) An MCP client using the SDK's default 60 s request timeout calls publish_post with the approved confirm token for a 300 MB video from a localPath. The model sees only "Request timed out" and calls publish_post again with the same arguments and token. The token is an HMAC over the unchanged payload and is not single-use, so the gate passes. check.reasoning:
The defect is real, but the trigger in the finding is wrong for this user's actual MCP client.

What the code really does:
- The handler ignores cancellation. server.ts:227 is `async (args) =>` and never takes `extra`. server.ts:288-290 calls `publishService().publish(draft, chosen.map(targetFor), { idempotencyKeyFor: ... })` with no `signal`. PublishService already accepts a signal (publish-service.ts:117), and the adapter would honour it (youtube.ts:618-625: 'The upload was cancelled before it finished. Nothing was published.'). From MCP that code is never reached.
- Cancelling only hides the result. In SDK 1.30.0 (dist/esm/shared/protocol.js), `_oncancel` (169-175) aborts the handler's controller, and after the handler finishes, line 369 runs `if (abortController.signal.aborted) { return; }`. The upload still finishes and recordTarget still writes 'published' (server.ts:292-294). The client never gets the answer.
- The approval can be used again. policy.ts:401-410 only recomputes the HMAC, and decide() (440-447) lets any matching token through. The secret lasts for the whole process (376-381).
- Nothing removes the duplicate:
  - Each call makes a new Post row (server.ts:282; tenant-scope.ts:109-117 has no dedupe check).
  - The idempotency key `${post.id}:${connectionId}` changes with every call.
  - youtube.ts:53-57 says videos.insert has no idempotency, and only the worker guards against repeats.
- Scratch proof (scratchpad\review\cancel-ignored.test.mjs, passing): it uses the real SDK over InMemoryTransport and the real policy.ts. A client-side timeout cancels call 1 (`signals[0].aborted === true`), call 1's handler still finishes, and a retry with the same token passes the gate and runs again. Result: `uploads === 2`.

Correction to the trigger:
- The server is registered only in D:\My AI Works\.mcp.json, which is Claude Code's project config. There is no Claude Desktop config, and the Codex and Cursor configs do not list it.
- The installed Claude Code 2.1.286 binary calls `V.callTool(..., {signal:u, timeout:W, onprogress})`:
  - `W` = per-server timeout, else `MCP_TOOL_TIMEOUT`, else `To=1e8` ms (about 27.8 h). No override is set anywhere, so the SDK's 60 s default never applies.
  - MCP calls also move to the background after `ee=120000` ms.
  - Stdio servers have an idle timeout of `Po=1800000` ms (30 min), reset only by progress notifications. This server sends none.
- So the real triggers are:
  (a) The user presses Esc during the first 2 minutes. `pue()` passes the turn's abort to the call signal, and the SDK sends notifications/cancelled.
  (b) The user stops the background task.
  (c) The upload runs 30 minutes with no progress, for example about 2 GB at 10 Mbps. The client then reports 'sent no response or progress for 1800s; aborting'.
- In each case the upload keeps going. Until it finishes, list_posts shows the post with no targets, which looks like nothing went out. A retry with the still-valid token then starts a second videos.insert.
- Even if the user changes the text and approves again, the 'cancelled' first video still goes up.

Severity is medium:
- Until the audit (D5), YouTube duplicates are private. Once uploads are public they would be public duplicates.
- The same problem exists in the HTTP transport (tools.ts:220/296) and on the LinkedIn video path, though there it was already present before this change.
check.minimal_fix:
1. In apps/mcp/src/server.ts, change the publish_post callback to `async (args, extra) =>` and pass `signal: extra.signal` in the options to `publishService().publish(...)` at line 288. Make the same change in tools.ts:220/296.
2. Make an approval work only once per process. Keep an in-memory Map from confirm token to postId, filled when the gate passes. When the same token comes back, return 'Already sent as post <id>; check list_posts' and do not publish again. Do not just reject the token: decide() would hand back the identical token.
3. Refinement: in youtube.ts, stop honouring the abort once the final chunk has been sent. Otherwise a cancel during that last PUT reports 'Nothing was published' for a video that exists.
4. Optional: send progress notifications through `extra.sendNotification` while chunks upload. That keeps Claude Code's 30-minute idle timer reset. Note that Claude Code's hard per-call timeout is not extended by progress.

low.failure_scenario:
1. vault.withCredential finds the hour-long access token expired and calls refreshCredential, which calls #token.
2. fetch resolves with the headers, then the socket drops before the JSON body is read ('terminated' / ECONNRESET).

low.suggested_fix:
1. Wrap `response.text()` in try/catch in both #token and #get.
2. On failure, throw a GoogleOAuthError with failureClass 'transient' and the original error as cause.
3. Do not route it through classifyNetworkError: that returns 'permanent' for any error code it does not recognise.

low.failure_scenario: (a) Google's token endpoint sends its headers, then the connection drops while the body is being read. response.text() rejects with a plain `TypeError: terminated` that has no failureClass. The vault marks the YouTube connection needs_reauth ('refresh failed') and throws NeedsReauthError. The worker files the target as needs_reauth, the monitor's checkConnections goes CRITICAL, and the channel stays off until someone reconnects it. This is the 'one blip disables a working channel' case D14 was meant to prevent. (b) The owner rotates GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET, or the OAuth client is deleted and later restored. Every refresh then returns invalid_client, deleted_client or unauthorized_client, which is classified 'permanent'. The vault marks every Google connection needs_reauth, and the web accounts page marks the provider authorisation needs_reauth too. publish-service reports class 'credential' with no code, so MCP shows TOKEN_EXPIRED 'reconnect'. After the env is fixed, the provider auth still needs a full OAuth re-run. Every non-transient failure marks the account dead. google-provider.ts:357 `const text = await response.text()` sits outside the try at 345-355 that turns fetch failures into transient errors. google-errors.ts:171-175 returns `{ failureClass: 'permanent' }` for client errors, although its own comment calls them 'a problem with the app's own configuration: permanent, but not the person's token'. publish-service.ts:210-219 maps any NeedsReauthError to 'credential'.
low.suggested_fix: In GoogleOAuth.#token (and #get), wrap response.text() and the JSON parse so that a failed body read becomes a transient GoogleOAuthError. In the vault, mark needs_reauth only when the refresh failure's failureClass is 'credential'. Re-throw 'permanent' failures without marking, so they are reported but do not disable the account.
